title: Native Debugging, Symbols, Sanitizers, and Crash Reports Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies native debugging, symbols, sanitizers, and crash reports?
options: Bind every crash to exact build-ID symbols and use the appropriate sanitizer or debugger to prove and prevent the causal defect.
Ship sanitizer timings as release benchmarks
questions.answer: Bind every crash to exact build-ID symbols and use the appropriate sanitizer or debugger to prove and prevent the causal defect.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A successful native stack symbolication proves the displayed function caused the original memory corruption.
questions.explanation: Symbolicating an arm64 tombstone with symbols from another version or ABI can name the wrong function and misdirect the investigation.

questions.prompt: What does a native build ID join?
questions.answer: The exact shipped ELF binary and crash addresses to its matching symbol and source artifacts.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
